import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`calimero-sdk`'s `testing` feature is the harness: your app built as the real
`calimero:app` component, run on the real wasmtime engine with an in-memory
host (`crates/sdk/src/testing`). A passing test means what it means on a node.
The harness plays the node's executor: it applies a call's changes only when the
call ends `Ok`, seeds each logged run so tests repeat, and resolves event
audiences against the org you give it.

## Set up

```toml
[dependencies]
calimero-sdk = { .. }

[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dev-dependencies]
calimero-sdk = { .., features = ["testing"] }
calimero-app-build = { .. }
serde_json = "1"
```

`calimero-app-build` builds the crate into a component (`wasm32-wasip2`) for the
test. The component apps in core share a small helper for that
(`apps/kv-store/tests/common`).

## `TestApp`

`apps/kv-store/tests/harness.rs`:

```rust
use calimero_sdk::testing::{Failure, Org, TestApp};
use serde_json::json;

#[test]
fn set_get_len_remove() {
    let mut t = common::app(Org::new().members(["bob"]));
    t.as_("owner").call("set", json!({ "key": "k", "value": "v" })).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(t.as_("owner").view("get", json!({ "key": "k" })), Ok(json!("v")));
    assert_eq!(t.as_("owner").view("len", json!({})), Ok(json!("1")));
}
```

- `TestApp::new(component, org, now_ms)` creates the app; `init` runs as the
  owner.
- `Org::new().admins([..]).members([..]).guests([..]).teams([..])` sets the org
  the app sees through `env::org_role` and `env::in_team`.
- `t.as_(account).call(method, args)` / `.view(..)` run a method as `account`,
  with camelCase JSON arguments, the same as a client sends. The result is
  `Result<Value, Failure>`: `Failure::App { code, fields }` for an app error.
- `t.events_for(account)` lists the events `account` received, in order.
- `t.anonymous()` and `t.system()` call as a caller who is not signed in and as
  the node; `t.api_key(..)` as an API key.
- Time and timers: `t.set_time(ms)`, `t.advance(ms)`, `t.tick(timer)`.
- The outside world: `t.mock_http(..)` answers outbound HTTP, `t.mock_app(..)`
  stands in for another app, `t.take_xcalls()` / `t.deliver(..)` inspect and
  deliver cross-app messages, `t.add_file(..)` / `t.file(..)` seed and read
  files.

## Scenarios

A scenario is a JSON list of steps that the Rust harness, the TypeScript
harness and the node's cluster runner all run, so one file tests the app
everywhere. Each `scenarios/<name>.json` runs in the org its
`<name>.org.json` names.

```json
[
  { "as": "bob", "op": "call", "method": "getOrInsert",
    "args": { "key": "k", "value": "first" },
    "expect": { "ok": "first" },
    "events": { "bob": ["Inserted"] } }
]
```

- `op`: `call`, `view`, `tick` (a timer, always as the system), `advance`
  (milliseconds), `removeMember`, or `upgrade` in a migration scenario
  ([below](#upgrades-test-against-a-shipped-releases-state)).
- `as`: an account, `"@anonymous"` or `"@system"`; `"confirmed": true` adds the
  passkey step-up.
- `expect`: `{ "ok": value }`, `{ "error": code, "fields": {..} }`,
  `{ "trap": .. }`, `{ "confirmRequired": true }`, or
  `{ "refused": "<API code>" }` when the platform refuses before the app runs.
- `"save": "id"` stores a result; `"$id"` later in `args` or `expect` is
  replaced by it. `"@bob"` is the account `bob` as the app sees it.
- `events` lists, per account, every event name it has received so far.

Run them all from one test (`apps/kv-store/tests/scenarios.rs`):

```rust
use calimero_sdk::testing::run_scenario;

#[test]
fn every_scenario_passes() {
    for path in common::scenarios() {
        let mut t = common::app(common::org_of(&path));
        run_scenario(&mut t, &path).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{}: {e:#}", path.display()));
    }
}
```

## Upgrades: test against a shipped release's state

An upgrade switches an app's code and keeps its state, so the code you ship
next must read what every release still in use wrote
([Upgrades & state](/core/build/migrations/)). Test that against the real
thing: the signed `.mpk` you shipped, not today's code with an old version
number. The harness runs that release's component, lets a scenario write state
with it, upgrades to the build under test as a node does (code only, nothing
runs) and goes on with the same state.

Lay it out by release, beside `scenarios/`:

```text
releases/1.0.0.mpk          the bundle 1.0.0 shipped, committed as it was published
migrations/1.0.0.json       a scenario: steps on 1.0.0, { "op": "upgrade" }, steps on this build
migrations/1.0.0.org.json   its org, as for any scenario (optional)
tests/migrations.rs
```

`apps/kv-store/migrations/0.1.0.json`:

```json
[
  { "as": "owner", "op": "call", "method": "set", "args": { "key": "a", "value": "1" } },
  { "as": "bob", "op": "call", "method": "set", "args": { "key": "b", "value": "2" } },
  { "op": "upgrade" },
  { "as": "bob", "op": "view", "method": "entries", "args": {}, "expect": { "ok": { "a": "1", "b": "2" } } },
  { "as": "bob", "op": "call", "method": "updateIfExists", "args": { "key": "a", "value": "10" }, "expect": { "ok": true } }
]
```

`apps/kv-store/tests/migrations.rs` runs every one of them:

```rust
use calimero_sdk::testing::{release_component, run_migration};

#[test]
fn every_release_upgrades_to_this_build() {
    let dir = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"));
    for path in common::scenarios_in(&dir.join("migrations")) {
        let version = path.file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()).unwrap_or_default();
        let mpk = std::fs::read(dir.join("releases").join(format!("{version}.mpk"))).unwrap();
        let old = release_component(&mpk, None).unwrap();
        run_migration(&old, common::component(), common::org_of(&path), common::T0, &path)
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{}: {e:#}", path.display()));
    }
}
```

- `release_component(mpk, service)` (feature `releases`) is the component of
  `service` (`None` for a single-service release) in a signed `.mpk`, after the
  signature and digest checks a node makes on install.
- `run_migration(from, to, org, now_ms, path)` starts the app on `from`, runs
  the scenario, and switches to `to` at its one `{ "op": "upgrade" }` step;
  saved variables carry across it. It returns the `TestApp` for more asserts.
- `t.upgrade(component)` does the switch in a test of your own;
  `Refused { 400, "BAD_BUNDLE" }` for a component that cannot be prepared.

Turn the feature on beside `testing`:

```toml
[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dev-dependencies]
calimero-sdk = { .., features = ["testing", "releases"] }
```

When the new code cannot read the old state, the step that reads it fails and
names it:

```text
migrations/0.1.0.json: step 5: {"as":"bob","method":"entries","op":"view",..}:
expected ok {"a":"1","b":"2"}, got Ok(Object {})
```

Keep a release's files for as long as an instance may still run it: an
instance can skip releases, and every later build must read its state. The
step-by-step walk through a release is [Ship v2 of your app](/core/build/ship-v2/).

<Aside type="note" title="In the apps repository">
  An app there (`logic/crates/<service>/`) adds the same three things to its
  service crate: `releases/<version>.mpk`, the bundle its release workflow
  published for that version (download it once from the release and commit
  it), `migrations/<version>.json`, and a `tests/migrations.rs` like the one
  above, with `calimero-sdk`'s `releases` feature on its dev-dependency. Its
  `cargo test` then runs them with the app's scenarios; a multi-service
  release passes the service name to `release_component`.
</Aside>

## Unit tests on the host

Plain `#[test]`s may also call the app's state directly on the host target:
`env::mock` stands in for the host there. Actions, cross-app calls and outbound
HTTP answer an error outside a component; use `TestApp` for those.

<Aside type="note">
  The node's own tests run the same scenarios on a three-node cluster
  (`crates/node/tests/scenarios.rs`); see
  [Testing strategy](/core/contribute/testing/).
</Aside>
